scene_brief: Home kitchen at night after the over-spiced dinner and chiku-shopping walk. View from a slightly elevated diagonal so BOTH full dogs on floor AND counter top are visible. Neet stands naturally on all four paws facing counter, head tilted up intensely; Buddy sits properly beside him, paws grounded, neck and chest continuous, eyes tracking the cups with extraordinary stillness. Buddy uses the tidier photographed grooming of B15: short hanging ears, restrained pale moustache/brows, close dark torso. At counter edge are EXACTLY FOUR clearly separated drinking cups: TWO small dog portions and TWO regular human portions, not bowls yet. A cropped adult forearm and hand from Sagar at frame edge tilt a jug, thick golden-tan chiku shake flowing into one small cup; other three cups visible and partly filled. Stopped blender behind them, ordinary kitchen, no human face needed. Counter is supported, natural hand ownership, no extra cup or hands. No food on dogs yet, no spilled shake, no tongues slurping; this is the hushed expectant moment before bowls/ceremony. Comedy comes from both normally chaotic dogs being perfectly attentive to their counted shares.
placement_after: Neet watched the stream of shake, following the jug from cup to cup. Buddy sat very still except for his tail. This was going into four cups. He had counted.
alt_text: Both dogs watch four cups of chiku shake being filled with unusual, hopeful silence.
